data.cultural_impact: Yasrib, now known as Medina or Al-Madinah Al-Munawwara (The Radiant City), was the second community of Muslims founded by Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) after the migration from Makkah to Madinah. As a thriving cultural and historical city, it is regarded as the cradle of Islam, hosting significant events such as the first Islamic treaty, the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, and the establishment of the first Islamic state. The vibrant Islamic culture continues to sustain the city with its richliterature, art, and architectural marvels.
data.spiritual_significance: Yasrib symbolizes a community of believers striving for spiritual growth and perfection under the guidance of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). The city represents an invitation to all to seek knowledge, strive for righteousness, and build a just and equitable society. The name signifies a haven where one's soul could thrive, as it is indefinitely enriched through study and application of divine teachings and the practice of faith.

islamic_reference.note: Traditional Islamic name with deep spiritual significance in Islamic culture

historical_references.reference: Ibn Ishaq, Sirat Rasul Allah (The Life of Muhammad), translated by A. Guillaume. Page 189, 218. (1955)
historical_references.context: Yasrib became an important commercial center, and Muslims started to migrate there. It was during this period that the Prophet Muhammad sent his emigrant companions, the Sahabah, to Yasrib under the leadership of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh. The Muslims were able to buy lands and build mosques, and the city became known as Madinatul-Zahra (the Radiant City) or Medina (the City).

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End). Volume 3, page 143-149. (1373 H) The name Yasrib carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: During this period, Yasrib was a significant trading center. The Prophet Muhammad dispatched Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and some companions to Yasrib to establish a Muslim community there. The Muslims bought lands and built mosques, and Yasrib became known as Jannah (Garden) or Madinatun-Nabi (City of the Prophet). The name Yasrib was eventually replaced by these Islamic names.
